elements.element: A review or audit against Customer may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph states that any review or audit shall be conducted “not more than once in any 12 month period.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 30 days' prior notice of the review or audit.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires “30 days' prior” notice.

elements.element: The audit notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly requires “written notice.”

elements.element: The review or audit must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires the audit to occur “during normal business hours.”

elements.element: The review or audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly requires “an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires the auditor to be “bound by obligations of confidentiality.”

elements.element: If the underpayment does not exceed 5%, Vendor must bear all costs of an audit against Customer.
elements.evidence: For an audit requested by Vendor, the new paragraph makes the requesting party bear its own costs unless the 5% threshold is exceeded, while existing Section 9.8 permits Customer to recover its reasonable compliance costs from the requesting party.

elements.element: If the underpayment exceeds 5%, Vendor's obligation to bear all audit costs may cease.
elements.evidence: Although the new paragraph excepts the requesting party's obligation to bear “its costs” when underpayment exceeds 5%, it does not allocate those costs to Customer, and Section 9.8 continues to let the audited party recover its compliance costs from the requester regardless of underpayment. The intended cost-shifting exception is therefore incomplete and internally inconsistent.

elements.element: The auditor must have no direct access to Customer's systems.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph states that the audit “shall not include direct access to the audited Party's systems,” which covers Customer when Customer is audited.

elements.element: A review or audit against Customer may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling cap of not more than once in any 12-month period is at least as protective as once per year.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 15 days' prior notice of the review or audit.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires 30 days' prior written notice, exceeding the fallback notice period.

elements.element: If the underpayment does not exceed 10%, Vendor must bear all costs of an audit against Customer.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph purports to except the requester's cost obligation once underpayment exceeds 5%. Thus, for an underpayment above 5% but not above 10%, it does not preserve the fallback requirement that Vendor bear the audit costs.

elements.element: If the underpayment exceeds 10%, Vendor's obligation to bear all audit costs may cease.
elements.evidence: The operative trigger is 5%, not 10%. Moreover, even after the trigger, Section 9.8 continues to permit recovery of the audited party's compliance costs from the requester, so the cost exception is not fully implemented.

result.reason: Most procedural protections are implemented, but the cost-shifting mechanism is incomplete and conflicts with the retained reimbursement language in Section 9.8. The redline also adds an unrequested “off-site where possible” restriction and applies all new limits mutually to audits of any party rather than solely to audits against Customer. Accordingly, it reaches neither complete position, changes more than necessary, and introduces uncertainty into the existing cost allocation.
